notes.summary: Profit & Loss with discount is one of the most asked arithmetic topics (1–3 questions). Always work with CP as the base for profit and MP as the base for discount.

concepts.title: Profit and loss
concepts.body: Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP. Profit% and Loss% are always on CP. SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100.

concepts.title: Discount
concepts.body: Discount is always on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100. Two successive discounts a% and b% equal a single discount of a + b − ab/100%.

concepts.title: Dishonest dealer
concepts.body: If a dealer gives less weight, Gain% = (Error / True value given) × 100 = error/(true − error) × 100.

varieties.name: Profit / loss percent
varieties.how: Use CP as base. Find CP from SP using the ratio (100 ± P%).

example.q: An item bought for ₹ 250 is sold for ₹ 300. Profit %?
MP is 50% above CP and a 20% discount is given. Profit %?
A shopkeeper uses a 950 g weight for 1 kg and sells at CP. Gain %?

tips: Profit% on CP; discount% on MP: never mix bases.
traps: Equal profit and loss % on two items sold at the same SP always gives a net LOSS of (x/10)<sup>2</sup>%.
Gain% in a false-weight question is error/950, not error/1000.

questions.q: A man buys an article for ₹ 400 and sells it for ₹ 460. What is his profit percentage?
The marked price of a watch is ₹ 800. A discount of 15% is given. What is the selling price?

A shopkeeper sells an article for ₹ 720 at a loss of 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 15%?
A dishonest shopkeeper claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a weight of 900 g instead of 1 kg. What is his gain percentage?
questions.solution:
He gives 900 g but charges for 1000 g.
Error = 100 g.
Gain% = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9 %.

questions.q: A trader allows a discount of 10% on the marked price and still gains 26%. By what percent is the marked price above the cost price?
